To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a non-renormalizable coupling between the Higgs field and Higgsinos can enhance the Higgss to diphoton decays in supersymmetric models, and that the Higgsino loop diagram can also enhance the Higgs diphoton decay in the non-perturbatibe Higgs model.
we suggest two models to enhance the diphoton channel of the Higgs boson.
a possibility of enhancing the Higgs to two photon decay rate is studied in a model with non-renormalizable Higgs term and in a SUSY QCD model where a strong dynamics generates Higgsino mass terms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possibility of enhancement of diphtoton decay rate in the non-perturbatively extended Higgs model.
a possibility of enhancement of the diphoton Higgs decay in supersymmetric models.
a non-perturbation Higgs sector which can give rise to a constructive contribution to diphoton Higgs decay amplitude and the enhancement of the decay width can be obtained in the models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a non-perturative model with a strong dynamics is a more promising model than a perturbative one to explain the enhancement of the diphoton Higgs decay width.
a significant enhancement of the diphoton branching fraction is possible if there is a new particle with a mass around 125 GeV, which couples to a photon.

there are some models which can explain the observed enhancement of diphotons in a context of supersymmetry, but a model with a non-renormalizable Higgs sector would be disfavored due to the low energy limit of the model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a non-pertubative Higgs model is a possible candidate to explain the enhanced Higgs to diphoon decay width.
the Higgs to two photons decay rate can be enhanced by a factor of about 10 if the Higgsino is light.

the enhancement of diphotons in the Higgs decay is not necessarily in conflict with the perturbative models and a non-pertubative model can be a possible candidate for a model to explain the excess of diphoton events in the Higgs search at the LHC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Higgs to di-photon decay width can be enhanced in a non-pertubative model with an extension of the Higgs sector.
the Higgs coupling can be enhanced by a loop diagram via a Higgsino and the diphoton signal can be enhanced in the non-perturbatively generated model.
a non-pertubative dynamics can be a possible origin of a large Higgs to dipphoton decay width.
